previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of multiple coronary stents was admitted for evaluation of recurrent chest pain. The pain, occurring at rest and relieved by nitroglycerin, was consistent with unstable angina. Cardiac catheterization revealed a 90% stenosis in the distal right coronary artery, where a drug-eluting stent was successfully placed. The patient tolerated the procedure well, with resolution of symptoms. He also had a minimally displaced right patellar fracture from a recent fall, managed non-operatively with bracing. He received dialysis during admission, and his medications were continued without complications. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up with cardiology, primary care, and orthopedics, and to maintain a heart-healthy diet and daily weight monitoring.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with unstable angina pectoris
Other fracture of right patella, initial encounter for closed fracture
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft

INDICATION:  History: ___ with chills  // Eval for PNA

TECHNIQUE:  Chest PA and lateral

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___

FINDINGS: 

Bilateral interstitial opacities likely represent interstitial edema.  There
is no new focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. 
Cardiomegaly persists.  The mediastinal and hilar contours are unchanged. 
Leftward scoliosis of the thoracic size stable.

IMPRESSION: 

Cardiomegaly and interstitial opacities, likely due to interstitial edema.  If
the diagnosis is in doubt clinically, followup radiographs after diuresis may
be helpful to exclude the possibility of an atypical interstitial pneumonia.

AP upright and lateral views of the chest provided.

There has been no significant change in the appearance of the chest.  There is
persistent interstitial opacity noted diffusely throughout both lungs likely
representing interstitial pulmonary edema.  No large effusion or pneumothorax.
Cardiomediastinal silhouette appears stable.  No acute osseous abnormalities. 
Chronic left mid/shaft clavicle deformity.

IMPRESSION: 

No significant change in diffuse interstitial opacity likely reflecting
interstitial pulmonary edema.
